title: Recombee — AI personalisation and search

slides.title: Recombee — AI personalisation and search
slides.notes: Who we are in one sentence: an AI personalisation and search engine that runs at scale and efficiently — most of our inference runs on CPU today because for our tasks it gives the best performance per price, GPUs where they pay off — with a university research lab behind it. First what we sell and to whom: three products and ten domains. Then the research behind them, and then what we could do for you.
slides.summary: Recombee in one deck: the products (recommendations, search, insights), the ten domains it specialises in with media and commerce side by side, the research behind it and an engine efficient by design.

slides.title: One engine: recommendations, search and insights
slides.body:
![[f-products|128%]]

> One engine for every placement — the client keeps the rules, we keep the models getting better.
slides.notes: What we sell, from the bottom up. More than a thousand servers in four regions — the US, Canada, Europe and Australia. On them runs the Recombee cloud: one distributed engine with more than a hundred models that learn in real time, thirty thousand recommendations a second. And that one engine powers all three products. Recommendations: every row of a homepage, similar items, what to watch or read next, the emails and push messages. Search that understands what a query means and ranks the results by each user's taste. And insights: live KPIs for every placement, with A/B tests built in. How clients steer it and plug it in comes on the next two slides.
slides.summary: What Recombee sells, as a stack built from the bottom: 1,000+ servers in four regions (US, Canada, EU, Australia), the distributed Recombee cloud running on them (one engine, 100+ models learning in real time, 30,000 recommendations a second), and the three products it powers, coming in one after another: Recommendations (1:1 homepage rows and feeds, similar items, watch next, personal emails and push, learning from every click live), personalised semantic Search (what a query means, ranked by each user's taste; quick search, faceted browsing) and Insights (live KPIs for every placement, A/B tests built in, segments, trends, retention). Light rises from the servers through the cloud into each product; the server lights blink.

slides.title: A few steps to personalisation
slides.body:
![[f-steps|120%]]

> Data in, in real time — a scenario per placement — personalisation out everywhere, and every result back into analytics.
slides.notes: How it works, the way our website draws it. A client sends two things: the catalogue — items and users, with their text and images — and the interactions, live as they happen and the history. Both flow into the engine in real time. For each placement the client sets up a scenario: what kind of recommendation, which logic, filters and boosters, constraints. Out come the homepage, search, newsletters, push, similar items, watch next — one engine behind all of them. And every result flows back into analytics, so the client sees what each placement earns.
slides.summary: How data flows through Recombee, after the "A Few Steps to Personalization" schema of recombee.com: 1 send data — the catalogue (items and users, with text and images) and interactions (live and history) stream into the engine in real time; 2 set up scenarios — recommendation type and logic, filters and boosters, constraints, with analytics and insights; 3 get personalisation — a personalised homepage and search, newsletters, push notifications, similar items, watch next, read next, others also bought and more; 4 check results — every placement reports back into analytics.

slides.title: Ten domains, one engine
slides.body:
![[f-domains|134%]]

> The same engine wins in media and in commerce — the domain changes the data, not the product.
slides.notes: Where we specialise. The top row is media and entertainment: FTV Prima's video, streaming platforms built by Diagnal — and DAZN in sport — The Telegraph in news, Audiomack in music, 9GAG for user content. The bottom row is commerce and marketplaces: retail, classifieds, real estate, jobs, travel and deals. Each number comes from a published case study on our website.
slides.summary: The ten domains of recombee.com, each with its picture from the website and a result from a public case study: video and pay-TV (FTV Prima, +34 % video views), sport and streaming (Diagnal, +35 % playbacks across video platforms; also DAZN), news and publishing (The Telegraph, +35 % CTR in an A/B test), music and audio (Audiomack, +206 % plays from recommendations), UGC and entertainment (9GAG, +37 % post views); e-commerce and retail (Design Group, +52 % purchases), P2P marketplaces (Pet Media Group, +17 % of visitors buy), real estate (Crexi, +40 % buy actions), jobs and recruitment (Infostud, +32 % applications), travel and deals (Slickdeals, +70 % CTR to deal pages). Also Perlego, Autohaus Kunzmann, Cooklist and Sleepiest.

slides.title: Sport & live events: every fan's favourite platform
slides.body:
![[f-sport|128%]]

> Sport is where personalisation has to be live — and where we already run at global scale.
slides.notes: Sport is our spearhead in media. Homepage rows built for each fan — live matches, replays, the leagues and teams they follow. The model learns during the match, not overnight. Editors still steer: premium matches, sponsors, local leagues — and it stays one-to-one. Semantic search for queries like "goals this weekend". Personal highlight reels. DAZN runs this in more than two hundred markets, on every device.
slides.summary: What Recombee does for sports platforms (from the Sports one-pager): 1:1 homepage rows, real-time learning during the match, editorial control, semantic sports search, personal highlight reels, trending in your country; a quote of Christoph Haas, EVP Product & Platform Engineering at DAZN, with DAZN's logo. Every card moves the way its screen would: the focus hops along the rows, a slider boosts premium content, a query is typed and its results appear, reels scroll.

slides.title: Video, news & music: a feed for every viewer, reader and listener
slides.body:
![[f-dom-media|128%]]

> Media is where personalisation has to be fast — and efficient at every request.
slides.notes: Media is our home, next to sport. Broadcasters like FTV Prima, video platforms built by Diagnal: a homepage built for each viewer, the next episode while the credits roll. The Telegraph, where a new article has to reach the right readers within seconds, and search and recommendations run on one engine — they measured us against a competitor in an A/B test: thirty-five percent more clicks. Audiomack, where recommendations tripled monthly plays. What they share: catalogues change by the minute, traffic peaks during live events, every device counts. That is why our models are sparse and efficient — they answer in milliseconds, and most of them run on CPU, where the price-performance is best for this work.
slides.summary: What Recombee does for media, with mock-ups from recombee.com, each one moving: rows for each viewer (genres, moods, editors' picks), watch next, articles for each reader fresh within seconds of publishing, semantic article search ranked by each reader's interests, playlists and play next for every listener. What clients report (public case studies): Diagnal +35 % playbacks across video platforms, FTV Prima +34 % video views on its VOD, The Telegraph +35 % CTR in an A/B test against a competitor, Audiomack +206 % monthly plays, Sleepiest +42 % user retention.

slides.title: Recombee Research: 12 papers accepted in 2026
slides.body:
![[f-research|128%]]

> Peer-reviewed, public and ours — the published work is at [recombee.com/research](https://www.recombee.com/research).
slides.notes: A word about where the products come from. Recombee Research and RecombeeLab — our joint lab with the Czech Technical University in Prague — had twelve papers accepted this year: at RecSys, UMAP, CIKM, WWW and IJCAI, with two best-paper nominations at UMAP. These are pages of papers we have already published: an industry-track paper at RecSys on embeddings ninety percent slimmer, the editorial analytics we built with The Telegraph, linear autoencoders at industrial scale, work at WWW and ICML. We fund PhD students who work on our production problems, and we open-source what we can. Everything published is on recombee.com/research.
slides.summary: Recombee Research and RecombeeLab, our joint lab with the Faculty of Information Technology of the Czech Technical University in Prague: 12 research papers accepted in 2026 at RecSys, UMAP, CIKM, WWW and IJCAI, two UMAP best-paper nominations; open source (ELSA, beeFormer, CompresSAE, RepSys); sponsor and co-organiser of RecSys. Pages of published papers scroll past, as recombee.com/research-publications shows them: The Future is Sparse (RecSys 2025, industry track), Lessons from The Telegraph (INRA at RecSys 2025), SAGEA (RecSys 2025), a linear next-basket model (RecSys 2025), shallow autoencoders at scale (ACM TORS 2025), risks in semantic search (UMAP 2025), beeFormer (RecSys 2024), curiosity detection (WWW 2024), deep matrix completion (ICML 2024), inductive matrix factorisation (AAAI 2023).

slides.title: Semantic IDs: what the leaders publish this year — and our breakthrough
slides.body:
![[f-sid-industry|128%]]

> The leaders bet on semantic IDs — our breakthrough beats them, and efficiently.
slides.notes: The hottest topic of recommender systems right now. Google started it with TIGER; YouTube now has Gemini write every video as a code. Spotify uses semantic IDs for podcast discovery, Meta in its ads ranking, Kuaishou serves a quarter of its traffic with one generative model built on them, Alibaba's maps predict your next place as a code. What they share: giant generative transformers that are heavy to train and to serve. We have a scientific breakthrough here that works markedly better than semantic IDs and those giant transformers — and it is efficient. The paper is under review at WWW, so that is all I can say today.
slides.summary: Semantic IDs are what the leaders of the field publish in 2025–2026: Google and YouTube (TIGER, 2023; PLUM, Gemini writes each video as a code: +4.96 % Shorts clicks), Spotify (GLIDE, podcast discovery on Home: up to +14.3 % new shows found), Meta and Instagram (semantic IDs in production ads ranking since 2025, and as ranking features), Kuaishou (OneRec, one generative model on semantic IDs: about a quarter of all traffic), Alibaba's Amap (Gwhere, the next place as a code: +5.83 % place clicks). The field decodes them with giant generative transformers — powerful, but heavy to train and to serve. Ours, only hinted at: a scientific breakthrough, under review at WWW, that works markedly better than semantic IDs and giant transformers — and it is efficient.

slides.title: Efficient by design: share meaning and experience, serve sparse
slides.body:
![[f-efficient|128%]]

> The best model for each database — on the hardware with the best price-performance.
slides.notes: Why efficiency matters. We serve thousands of databases; a GPU at every request would make cost grow with traffic. So we share what is cheap to share: frozen encoders and one sparse dictionary, computed once per item on CPU, and the experience of thousands of A/B tests — a small meta-model that predicts which algorithm wins for which data. Serving stays sparse and linear — thirty thousand recommendations a second — and today most of our inference runs on CPU: not on principle, but because for these tasks CPUs give us the best performance per price. GPUs do what they do best: training and the heavy encoders. And a CPU is only cheap when it is well used — keeping it busy is our job, not the client's.
slides.summary: Not one giant shared model (GPU at every request, months of training, no single winner); instead frozen encoders, one SAE dictionary and per-client adapters computed once per item on CPU, a meta-brain — a small model on metadata — that learns from our grid searches and A/B tests which algorithm wins for which data, and per-client A/B with the final say, run automatically.

slides.title: What we could do for you
slides.body:
- **Start with one placement** — the homepage, search, a feed or an e-mail. The catalogue and the interactions come in through our API or SDKs; no ML team is needed.
- **Prove it on your own KPI** — an A/B test against what runs today, on the number you care about.
- **Grow from there** — every placement on one engine, with models that keep improving and a team that keeps testing new ones.

> One placement first, one number that proves it — then the rest.
slides.notes: What this would look like for you. We would not start with everything: one placement, the one where you most want to see a difference. You send us the catalogue and the interactions; the models learn from your own data. Then an A/B test against what you run today, on the number you care about. If it wins, we grow placement by placement — all on one engine.
slides.summary: Three steps to personalisation for you: start with one placement — the homepage, search, a feed or an e-mail — with the catalogue and interactions sent through the API or SDKs; prove it in an A/B test against what runs today, on the KPI that matters most; then grow to every placement on one engine, with models that keep improving.

slides.title: Thank you
slides.notes: Thank you. The case studies, the research and the documentation are all on recombee.com.
slides.summary: Thank you, with the swarm of the cover: bees carry items from the catalogue round the engine to people, new items arrive and are sniffed out and carried to the people they are for, and the Recombee mark turns now and then. Recombee's logo, next to the customer's when the deck has it, and how to reach Pavel Kordík: pavel.kordik@recombee.com.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1000 414.9" font-family="Inter,'Inter Display',system-ui,-apple-system,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif">
<style>
.pk-a{animation-duration:.9s;animation-timing-function:cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1);animation-fill-mode:both}
.pk-pop{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation-name:pop}
.pk-fade{animation-name:fade}
.pk-up{animation-name:up}
.pk-down{animation-name:down}
.pk-left{animation-name:left}
.pk-right{animation-name:right}
.pk-grow{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:left center;animation-name:grow;animation-duration:1.3s}
.pk-growy{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center bottom;animation-name:growy;animation-duration:1.2s}
.pk-ring{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:ring 2.8s ease-out infinite}
.pk-breathe{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:breathe 3.4s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-glow{animation:glow 3s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-blink{animation:blink 2.2s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-trav{animation:trav 2.6s linear infinite}
.pk-hop{animation:hop 3.6s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-orbit{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 14s linear infinite}
.pk-orbitr{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 20s linear infinite reverse}
@keyframes pop{0%{opacity:0;transform:scale(.3)}65%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1.06)}100%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1)}}
@keyframes fade{from{opacity:0}to{opacity:1}}
@keyframes up{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(18px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateY(0)}}
@keyframes down{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(-18px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateY(0)}}
@keyframes left{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(-24px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateX(0)}}
@keyframes right{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(24px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateX(0)}}
@keyframes grow{from{transform:scaleX(0)}to{transform:scaleX(1)}}
@keyframes growy{from{transform:scaleY(0)}to{transform:scaleY(1)}}
@keyframes ring{0%{transform:scale(.7);opacity:.85}100%{transform:scale(2.5);opacity:0}}
@keyframes breathe{0%,100%{transform:scale(1)}50%{transform:scale(1.06)}}
@keyframes glow{0%,100%{opacity:.35}50%{opacity:.9}}
@keyframes blink{0%,100%{opacity:1}50%{opacity:.35}}
@keyframes trav{0%{transform:translate(0px,0px);opacity:0}12%{opacity:1}86%{opacity:1}100%{transform:translate(var(--dx),var(--dy));opacity:0}}
@keyframes hop{0%,55%,100%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}70%{transform:translate(0px,-10px)}85%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}}
@keyframes spin{from{transform:rotate(0deg)}to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
.pk-beam{animation:rsbeam 3.4s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) infinite}
.pk-shine{animation:rsshine 5s linear infinite}
.pk-spinc{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:spin 9s linear infinite}
.pk-float{animation:rsfloat 7s ease-in-out infinite}
@keyframes rsbeam{0%{stroke-dashoffset:24}60%,100%{stroke-dashoffset:-100}}
@keyframes rsshine{from{stroke-dashoffset:100}to{stroke-dashoffset:0}}
@keyframes rsfloat{0%,100%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}50%{transform:translate(0px,-9px)}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{animation:none!important}.pk-trav,.pk-orbit,.pk-orbitr,.pk-bee,.pk-take,.pk-hit,.pk-beam,.pk-shine,.pk-sweep{display:none}}

<style>
.pk-a{animation-duration:.9s;animation-timing-function:cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1);animation-fill-mode:both}
.pk-pop{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation-name:pop}

.pk-up{animation-name:up}
.pk-down{animation-name:down}

.pk-trav{animation:trav 2.6s linear infinite}
.pk-hop{animation:hop 3.6s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-orbit{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 14s linear infinite}
.pk-orbitr{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 20s linear infinite reverse}

.pk-shine{animation:rsshine 5s linear infinite}

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1000 360" font-family="Inter,'Inter Display',system-ui,-apple-system,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif">
<style>
.pk-a{animation-duration:.9s;animation-timing-function:cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1);animation-fill-mode:both}
.pk-pop{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation-name:pop}
.pk-fade{animation-name:fade}
.pk-up{animation-name:up}
.pk-down{animation-name:down}
.pk-left{animation-name:left}
.pk-right{animation-name:right}
.pk-grow{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:left center;animation-name:grow;animation-duration:1.3s}
.pk-growy{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center bottom;animation-name:growy;animation-duration:1.2s}
.pk-ring{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:ring 2.8s ease-out infinite}
.pk-breathe{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:breathe 3.4s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-glow{animation:glow 3s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-blink{animation:blink 2.2s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-trav{animation:trav 2.6s linear infinite}
.pk-hop{animation:hop 3.6s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-orbit{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 14s linear infinite}
.pk-orbitr{transform-box:view-box;animation:spin 20s linear infinite reverse}
@keyframes pop{0%{opacity:0;transform:scale(.3)}65%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1.06)}100%{opacity:1;transform:scale(1)}}
@keyframes fade{from{opacity:0}to{opacity:1}}
@keyframes up{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(18px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateY(0)}}
@keyframes down{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(-18px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateY(0)}}
@keyframes left{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(-24px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateX(0)}}
@keyframes right{from{opacity:0;transform:translateX(24px)}to{opacity:1;transform:translateX(0)}}
@keyframes grow{from{transform:scaleX(0)}to{transform:scaleX(1)}}
@keyframes growy{from{transform:scaleY(0)}to{transform:scaleY(1)}}
@keyframes ring{0%{transform:scale(.7);opacity:.85}100%{transform:scale(2.5);opacity:0}}
@keyframes breathe{0%,100%{transform:scale(1)}50%{transform:scale(1.06)}}
@keyframes glow{0%,100%{opacity:.35}50%{opacity:.9}}
@keyframes blink{0%,100%{opacity:1}50%{opacity:.35}}
@keyframes trav{0%{transform:translate(0px,0px);opacity:0}12%{opacity:1}86%{opacity:1}100%{transform:translate(var(--dx),var(--dy));opacity:0}}
@keyframes hop{0%,55%,100%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}70%{transform:translate(0px,-10px)}85%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}}
@keyframes spin{from{transform:rotate(0deg)}to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
.pk-beam{animation:rsbeam 3.4s cubic-bezier(.45,0,.55,1) infinite}
.pk-shine{animation:rsshine 5s linear infinite}
.pk-spinc{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:spin 9s linear infinite}
.pk-float{animation:rsfloat 7s ease-in-out infinite}
@keyframes rsbeam{0%{stroke-dashoffset:24}60%,100%{stroke-dashoffset:-100}}
@keyframes rsshine{from{stroke-dashoffset:100}to{stroke-dashoffset:0}}
@keyframes rsfloat{0%,100%{transform:translate(0px,0px)}50%{transform:translate(0px,-9px)}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{animation:none!important}.pk-trav,.pk-orbit,.pk-orbitr,.pk-bee,.pk-take,.pk-hit,.pk-beam,.pk-shine,.pk-sweep{display:none}}

.pk-tybee{offset-rotate:auto;animation-name:tyFly;animation-timing-function:linear;animation-iteration-count:infinite}
.pk-tytake,.pk-tyhit{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;opacity:0;animation-timing-function:linear;animation-iteration-count:infinite}
.pk-tytake{animation-name:tyTake}
.pk-tyhit{animation-name:tyHit}
.pk-tyshim{animation-name:tyDash;animation-timing-function:linear;animation-iteration-count:infinite}
.pk-tybreathe{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:tyBreathe 3.4s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-tyglow{animation:tyGlow 3s ease-in-out infinite}
.pk-tyspin{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:tySpin 16s ease-in-out 1s infinite}
.pk-tysniffer{offset-rotate:auto;opacity:0;animation-duration:16s;animation-timing-function:linear;animation-iteration-count:infinite}
.pk-tywing{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;animation:tyWing .16s ease-in-out infinite alternate}
.pk-tyfresh{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;opacity:0;animation:tyFresh 16s ease-out infinite}
.pk-tyhalo{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;opacity:0;animation:tyHalo 16s ease-out infinite}
.pk-tyrel{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;opacity:0;animation:tyRel 16s ease-out infinite}
.pk-tygift{opacity:0;animation:tyGift 16s ease-out infinite}
